_readme: The gate contract, executed by BOTH languages.
monitor/gates.py decides what reaches a queue; webapp/lib/gating/dispose.ts
decides what the profile preview PROMISES will reach it. Two implementations
of one rule, and the failure they produce when they drift is silent: the app
tells somebody their new profile qualifies 61 postings and the engine gates a
different 61. This file is what makes that a CI failure instead.
tests/monitor/test_gate_corpus.py runs every case through Python.
webapp/tests/unit/gate-corpus.test.ts runs the same cases through TypeScript.
Neither implementation may add a branch without a case here, and the case is
written first. Seeded from tests/monitor/test_gates.py (one case per
assertion) plus acceptance criteria 1-8 and edge case G17.
`config` and `row` are PARTIAL. Missing config keys take `defaults` below;
a missing row key is the empty string, which is what `row.get(k, '')` gives
_defaults_readme: GateConfig's dataclass defaults, spelled out so both languages assert
against one copy. Duplicating them silently is how a port drifts on the
branch nobody writes a case for: `yoe_max` defaulting to 5 in TypeScript
would pass every case that names it and be wrong for every case that does
_kinds_readme: The closed set of disposition_reason KINDS (docs/PRODUCT-SPEC.md A2). Both
suites assert every kind appears in at least one case AND that no case
produces a kind outside it, so a gate rule added on one side with no corpus
row fails rather than going untested in both.

cases.why: the baseline: a US posting inside the YoE bar carries an EMPTY reason, not a cheerful one
acceptance criterion 1 — the reason names the country, so the UI can say which one
a posting nobody could place is not a US posting; the default policy says so
geo_unknown=keep must fall THROUGH to the later gates, not short-circuit to qualified
acceptance criterion 2 — a remote role with no stated origin is worth a look
edge case G17: remote does NOT launder a foreign anchor. Dropping the country check for remote rows would pass every other geo case
a human types US in a Config cell; geo.enrich writes United States. Both sides canonicalise or the profile filters everything
the alias table is applied to the ROW too, case-folded
the alias table has a second entry; a port that hardcoded only the US aliases passes every case above
remote is a three-token truthy set, upper-cased. YES is one of them
and so is the string 1 — the sheet writes it that way
the set is CLOSED. Treating any non-empty string as truthy would make `false` mean remote
U+001F is whitespace to Python's str.strip() and NOT to JavaScript's trim(). A port using trim() reports geo:India\u001f and the UI prints a control character
the same divergence the other way: U+FEFF IS stripped by trim() and is NOT whitespace to Python. Both directions have to be pinned or the port drifts on whichever one nobody wrote
dad's Chicagoland search: the metro he follows reaches him
the reason names the metro, so the preview can say which one is doing the filtering
in-country but unplaceable reuses the geo policy rather than inventing a second knob
the same knob in its other position; a port hardcoding `filter` passes the case above
acceptance criterion 3 — a remote role is location-independent and a local search still wants it
the national search: no metros configured must not filter on metro at all
ordering: a foreign row is geo-filtered before the metro gate is reached, which is why the binding constraint is computed by relaxation and not by counting reasons
the sheet pads cells; a padded metro must still match the list
and so is the configured one — a trailing space typed into a wizard chip must not silently filter the metro out
acceptance criterion 4 — the reason carries both numbers so the copy can name the limit
the comparison is strictly greater. An off-by-one here filters every posting that asks for exactly the user's ceiling
acceptance criterion 5 — an untagged row is not judged, it waits
the proxy fires only on the yoe-unknown path, and the reason carries the row's own spelling
the proxy is an exact match against the list, not a substring sweep over every seniority word
a finance-ladder profile sets keep precisely because the PM seniority proxy is wrong there — a Director of FP&A is a target, not a filter
no-jd:/failed: mean the tagger gave up; parking those as needs-info forever hides real postings behind a fetch failure
the second sentinel. A port special-casing only `no-jd:` passes the case above
an unparseable cell is unknown, never zero and never a crash — even against a set ceiling
int(float('4.9')) is 4, not 5. Rounding instead of truncating filters a posting that asks for four-and-a-bit years from a four-year ceiling
05 parses as 5 and the reason still says 05. Formatting the parsed value would change a string the digest and the UI both read
the comparison folds case; the reason quotes the posting verbatim so a human recognises it
Python casefold()s both sides: 'Straße' folds to 'strasse'. JavaScript toLowerCase() does not, so a bare toLowerCase() port silently stops matching

pins the DEFAULT rather than a value the case names — the default ceiling is UNSET (RM-40 vault audit Step 4: a profile that never stated one must not inherit anybody's), so a stated YoE qualifies. A port defaulting to any number filters this row
an explicit null ceiling is the same OFF state as an absent one — a port reading null as 0 filters everything, reading it as NaN crashes

#251 review: JS Number('') is 0, so a whitespace-only ceiling minted an entry-level-only filter nobody set. Unified semantics — blank INCLUDING whitespace is the OFF state in both languages (Python normalizes in GateConfig.__post_init__, where a raw whitespace string previously raised in from_user_config's int(); the sheet validator already landed None; TS strips before Number in toIntOrNull)
the default profile excludes NO seniority. A port seeding one person's exclusion list would filter another profile's Director roles on day one
an empty chip left behind in the wizard must not become a country nothing matches
acceptance criterion 6
acceptance criterion 7 — judged on the TOP, because judging on the bottom filters out most real negotiating ranges
acceptance criterion 8 — ~48% of live postings state nothing, so defaulting to filter deletes half the feed
'Competitive' must not read as $0 and vanish under any floor
the explicit opt-in half of criterion 8
criterion 8's last clause: a row has not been given its comp yet, so filtering it for not stating one is judging the engine's backlog
$45/hour must be unknown, not $45k. Reading it as a salary filters every contract posting under any floor
comp_min 0 means the gate does not run at all — not that everything clears a $0 floor (which would be the same answer here and a different one for comp_unknown=filter)
the k-suffixed shape, which _to_k must NOT divide by 1000
the same shape on the filtering side, so a port that treated every k value as unknown could not pass both
'$150k+' has no top; the gate judges on the floor rather than treating the range as unknown
'up to $100k' is a real refusal, not an unknown
the second most common real shape in the feed. A hyphen-only split reads it as one number
'USD' between the numbers is common and must not become a third value
MIN_PLAUSIBLE_K drops '$5 - $9' to unknown rather than filtering the row as a $9k job
_to_k treats a bare 150 as $150k and 150000 as $150k; both have to land on the same number
Python's :g renders 122.5 as 122.5 and 120.0 as 120. A port using toFixed(1) writes 'comp:<120.0k' and every reason string in the UI and the digest changes

Python's :g is 6 SIGNIFICANT digits, so 12.3456789 renders as 12.3457. The two existing floors (120 and 122.5) are both reproduced by a bare String(), so a port using it passed them both — this is the case that separates formatG from String()

The configured token ends in a NON-final sigma; the posting ends in a capital one. Python casefolds both to the same sigma, and JavaScript toLowerCase() renders a word-final capital sigma as FINAL sigma — so a port without the fold compares two different strings and stops matching. The asymmetry is the whole point: a token written with final sigma on both sides passes either way, which is how the first version of this case failed to discriminate. 313 codepoints fold like this and the port's docstring used to claim none did
GateConfig swallows a non-numeric floor rather than raising. A bad Config cell must not take the gate down
and so does a null, which is what an unset jsonb key deserialises to
the other side of the same coercion: a floor that arrives as a string still binds
the token is matched inside the work model string, which is free text from the tagger
the reason is the CONFIG token after __post_init__ case-folds it, not the posting's wording. A port echoing the row's text writes 'work-model:Onsite — Austin, TX'
the negative control: the gate must not fire on every work model once any token is configured
'Hybrid — Chicago' contains neither token and must survive
an untagged work model is not an onsite one; matching '' against a token list would filter every row before it is tagged
both gates would fire; the reason proves which one short-circuits. This is the whole reason the binding constraint is computed by relaxation
a reason histogram would credit geo and never see the comp floor behind it
the last short-circuit pair: a row failing both reports comp
